name: Census ACS 5-Year: Vacancy Status (tables B25002/B25004)
granularity: tract (aggregated to NTA by the existing adapter)
license: US Census Bureau public data, no restrictions on reuse

correlation.note: app/research/evaluate_series.py (Phase 4) doesn't exist yet in this repo, so no quantitative lead/lag or correlation check was run this pass. The case here rests on directly replacing a hardcoded constant with a real, neighborhood-varying measurement, which is independently verifiable (sanity-check against known high-vacancy vs low-vacancy NYC neighborhoods once loaded).

recommendation_summary: census_acs.py already pulls ACS variables by tract and aggregates to NTA using the same CENSUS_API_KEY and tract-relationship machinery this needs; adding a couple of variables to the VARS dict is a small diff to an adapter that already exists, not a new Source. It replaces investment.py's hardcoded vacancy_pct=0.05 — applied identically to every property today — with an actual per-neighborhood rental vacancy rate, and because ACS is national, it works for the project's any-US-neighborhood goal without extra code. Formula matters here: the correct rental vacancy rate is B25004_002E / (B25003_003E + B25004_002E + B25004_003E) — for-rent-vacant divided by (renter-occupied + for-rent-vacant + rented-but-not-occupied) — the standard ACS/DP04 definition. B25003_003E ('renters') is already in census_acs.py's VARS. A naive vacant/total-units formula (e.g. B25002_003E/B25002_001E, or even B25004_002E/B25002_001E) divides by all housing units including owner-occupied, which understates rental vacancy badly in owner-heavy neighborhoods.
